anomalies.observed: On the Microcontroller sheet (mcu.kicad_sch), the right-hand side of the ESP32-C3-MINI-1 (U1) shows 'GPIO4/ADC1_CH4' as pin 14 and 'GPIO5/ADC2_CH0' as pin 15. The net labels carried away from those two pins are 'SCK' on the pin-14 (GPIO4) row and 'CS0' on the pin-15 (GPIO5) row; the label stack reads SCK, CS0, CS1, CS2, SO down the pin group.
anomalies.expected: The specification states the shared SPI clock must be on GPIO5 and the first thermocouple chip-select CS0 on GPIO4: 'SPI2 on GPIO5/GPIO10, CS pins GPIO4/6/7' (firmware main.rs: sck GPIO5, miso GPIO10, CS GPIO4/GPIO6/GPIO7). GPIO4 should therefore be CS0 and GPIO5 should be SCK.

evidence.quote: SPI2 on GPIO5/GPIO10, CS pins GPIO4/6/7
each chip has its own independent chip-select: `~{CS}` (pin 6) on `U2`/`U3`/`U4` goes to separate nets `CS0`/`CS1`/`CS2`, driven by ESP32 GPIO4/GPIO6/GPIO7 respectively.
Microcontroller sheet, U1: 'GPIO4/ADC1_CH4  14' tied to net SCK and 'GPIO5/ADC2_CH0  15' tied to net CS0

anomalies.impact: Firmware drives the clock on GPIO5 and CS0 on GPIO4. With these two nets cross-wired on the board, the three MAX31855 devices would be clocked on their ~CS inputs and selected on their SCK inputs, so no valid thermocouple word would ever be shifted out; every zone would read as a thermocouple fault and the oven could not run.

parsed.summary: The ESP32-C3 SPI assignment appears cross-wired relative to the intended design: the schematic attaches net SCK to GPIO4 (pin 14) and net CS0 to GPIO5 (pin 15), whereas the specification/firmware require SCK on GPIO5 and CS0 on GPIO4, which would break all three MAX31855 thermocouple reads. All other component values and the power-mux, buck, heater-switch and thermocouple topologies match the specification.
